reply: s always negative and grows in magnitude with P, roughly like −P^1.5 with a weak exponential time factor. A linear basis of half-integer powers of P times t, t² reaches NMSE ≈ 5e-10, but it needs about 20 terms with messy coefficients, so it is not the closed form and exceeds the 10-parameter limit.

best.code:
import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    p=params
    s=np.sqrt(P)
    return (p[0] + p[1]*s + p[2]*P + p[3]*P*s + p[4]*P**2 + p[5]*P**2*s
            + p[6]*t*s + p[7]*t*P + p[8]*t*P*s + p[9]*t*P**2)
